question: What is the main way oxygen and carbon dioxide move across cell membranes?
explanation: Gases move naturally from areas of higher pressure to areas of lower pressure without needing energy from the cells. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body have a higher metabolic rate?

options.A: To support the growing placenta and baby
options.B: To make up for less lung capacity late in pregnancy
options.C: To prevent excess nitrogen in the blood
options.D: To cool down the mother's body temperature

explanation: The developing baby and placenta need constant energy and support, which increases the mother's overall oxygen use. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which way do oxygen molecules naturally travel during normal breathing?

options.A: From high pressure to low pressure
options.B: From the veins into the arteries
options.C: From low pressure to high pressure
options.D: From body tissues straight into the outside air

explanation: Gas always moves down a pressure gradient, traveling from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h2)

question: How does fluid buildup in the lungs affect gas exchange?

options.A: It reverses the pressure of oxygen and carbon dioxide
options.B: It stops the heart from pumping
options.C: It forces red blood cells to release all their hemoglobin
options.D: It increases the distance gases must travel, slowing down exchange

explanation: Extra fluid creates a wider barrier between the air sacs and blood vessels, making it harder for gases to pass through quickly. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h2)

question: Where does external respiration happen in the respiratory system?

options.A: Inside the walls of the heart
options.B: Across cell membranes in body tissues
options.D: Across the air sacs in the lungs

explanation: External respiration is the gas exchange between the air in the lung alveoli and the blood in the capillaries. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is happening when a pregnant woman's body unloads carbon dioxide into her lung alveoli?

options.A: Her lungs are preparing to make more oxygen
options.B: She is getting rid of waste gas from her blood
options.C: She is storing extra carbon dioxide to balance her blood pH
options.D: Carbon dioxide is turning into solid calcium

explanation: Carbon dioxide is a waste product from cellular work. It travels through the blood to the lungs so it can be breathed out. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h3)

question: How is most oxygen carried through the bloodstream to body tissues?

options.A: Bound to hemoglobin inside red blood cells
options.C: Floating as dissolved ions in serum
options.D: Dissolved as free gas in the plasma

explanation: Hemoglobin inside red blood cells acts as the main carrier, letting the blood transport much more oxygen than plasma could on its own. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h4)

question: What does hemoglobin do when blood reaches warm, active tissues making lots of carbon dioxide?

options.A: It changes color from bright red to white
options.B: It holds onto its oxygen even tighter
options.D: It releases its stored oxygen to the tissues

explanation: Active tissues generate heat and acid, signaling hemoglobin to drop off oxygen right where it is needed most. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h4)

question: In what main form is most carbon dioxide carried back to the lungs?

options.A: As dissolved bicarbonate in the plasma
options.C: As solid crystals in the blood vessels
options.D: As gas bubbles attached to platelets

explanation: The body turns most carbon dioxide into bicarbonate so it can travel safely in the blood plasma and help control body pH. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is turning carbon dioxide into bicarbonate important for the body?

options.A: It gives red blood cells energy to survive
options.B: It stops the liver from making too much cholesterol
options.C: It keeps blood pH within a safe range
options.D: It thickens the blood to prevent bleeding

explanation: The bicarbonate system acts as a chemical buffer, stopping blood from becoming too acidic by neutralizing extra hydrogen ions. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which way does oxygen move during internal respiration at the tissue level?

options.A: From the skin surface out into the air
options.B: From tissue cells into the lung alveoli
options.C: From venous blood into arterial circulation
options.D: From tiny blood vessels into surrounding tissue cells

explanation: Internal respiration means oxygen is being delivered from the capillaries into the working cells of the body. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which of these statements about internal respiration is FALSE?

options.A: Carbon dioxide moves from tissue cells into the blood
options.B: Oxygen levels are higher in the capillaries than in resting cells
options.C: Active tissues use up oxygen and make carbon dioxide waste
options.D: Gas exchange happens straight through the walls of the heart chambers

explanation: Gas exchange happens across the thin walls of tiny capillaries in the tissues, not through the thick muscular walls of the heart. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why does fetal hemoglobin pull oxygen away from the mother's blood in the placenta?

options.A: The placenta actively pumps oxygen using cellular energy
options.B: Maternal blood has no hemoglobin during late pregnancy
options.C: Fetal blood flows much slower than maternal blood
options.D: Fetal hemoglobin has a stronger pull on oxygen than adult hemoglobin

explanation: Fetal hemoglobin grabs onto oxygen more tightly than maternal hemoglobin, making sure the baby gets enough oxygen in the placenta. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h7)

question: What happens first to the fetus if a pregnant woman has severely low blood pressure?

options.A: Less oxygen reaches the placenta, which can cause fetal distress
options.B: The baby's birth weight and lung maturity suddenly increase
options.C: Blood flow direction in the umbilical cord reverses
options.D: Waste production stops inside the amniotic sac

explanation: Low maternal blood pressure reduces blood flow to the placenta, lowering the pressure gradient and starving the baby of needed oxygen. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h7)

question: What term describes a dangerously low level of oxygen in the mother's blood?
explanation: Hypoxemia specifically means there is a low amount of oxygen circulating in the arterial blood supply. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h8)

question: Why is placing a distressed pregnant woman on her left side a helpful nursing action?

options.A: It pushes air from her lungs straight into the placenta
options.B: It helps her bone marrow make more red blood cells
options.C: It takes pressure off major blood vessels and improves blood flow
options.D: It stops the baby from moving around in the amniotic fluid

explanation: Lying on the left side stops the heavy uterus from pressing on the inferior vena cava, keeping blood flowing well to the placenta. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h8)
